jsonld.name: 1031 Exchange Calculator
jsonld.description: Estimate the capital gains and depreciation recapture tax deferred by a like-kind exchange, check for taxable boot, and see the 45/180-day deadlines.

acceptedAnswer.text: A 1031 exchange lets you sell real property held for investment or business use and buy another like-kind property while deferring the capital gains and depreciation recapture tax, under Section 1031 of the Internal Revenue Code.

mainEntity.name: What is boot in a 1031 exchange?

acceptedAnswer.text: Boot is any value you receive that isn't like-kind property — cash you take out, or a reduction in mortgage debt that you don't offset with added cash. Boot is taxable up to the amount of your realized gain.

You must identify potential replacement properties in writing within 45 days of selling the relinquished property, and complete the purchase within 180 days of the sale or by your tax return due date (including extensions), whichever comes first.

mainEntity.name: Does a 1031 exchange eliminate the tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it defers it. The deferred gain reduces the basis of the replacement property and becomes taxable when you eventually sell without exchanging again — although heirs may receive a stepped-up basis.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a 1031 exchange on my home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on a main home. Section 1031 applies to real property held for investment or used in a business. A main home may instead qualify for the Section 121 exclusion of up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 married filing jointly).

mainEntity.name: Do I need a qualified intermediary for a 1031 exchange?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a delayed exchange, yes in practice. The sale proceeds must be held by a qualified intermediary so you never have access to the cash. Your own agents, such as your attorney, accountant or broker, and related parties cannot serve as the intermediary.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I miss the 45-day deadline?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you do not identify replacement property in writing within 45 days of the sale, the exchange generally fails and the gain is taxable in the year of the sale. The 45-day and 180-day periods run at the same time from the date you transfer the old property.

A reverse exchange means buying the replacement property before selling the old one. To qualify, an exchange accommodation titleholder holds title to one of the properties under a qualified exchange accommodation arrangement (Rev. Proc. 2000-37), and the same 45-day and 180-day periods apply.

mainEntity.name: Can I do a 1031 exchange on a vacation home or rental?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if it is held for investment or business use, not as a personal home. The IRS safe harbor in Rev. Proc. 2008-16 looks for 24 months of ownership with at least 14 days of fair rental in each of the two 12-month periods, and limited personal use.

mainEntity.name: Can I exchange into a property outside the United States?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. U.S. real property is not like-kind to real property outside the U.S., so a U.S. rental generally must be exchanged for U.S. real property.
Form 8824, filed with your tax return for the year of the transfer. It shows the realized and recognized gain, any boot, and the basis of the replacement property.

jsonld.name: How a delayed 1031 exchange works, step by step
jsonld.description: The five steps of a delayed 1031 like-kind exchange, from hiring a qualified intermediary to reporting on Form 8824.

step.name: Hire a qualified intermediary
step.text: Hire a qualified intermediary (QI) before you close the sale. The sale proceeds must go to the QI, not to you. Receiving the money yourself can disqualify the exchange or make it taxable boot.

step.name: Close the sale
step.text: Close the sale of the relinquished property. This starts both clocks.

step.name: Identify replacements by day 45
step.text: Identify replacement properties in a signed written notice sent to the QI or another party to the exchange.

step.name: Receive the replacement property
step.text: Receive the replacement property by the earlier of day 180 or your tax return due date, including extensions.

step.name: Report the exchange
step.text: Report the exchange on Form 8824 with your return for the year you transferred the property.
